summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring a gastrostomy tube and status post bypass reversal was readmitted five days after a prior discharge with recurrent constant abdominal pain localized to the G-tube site radiating to the left flank and repeated emesis with oral intake. She was managed conservatively with NPO and IV fluids, venting of the G-tube (which appeared patent), and symptom control with antiemetics and non-NSAID analgesia while continuing gastric mucosal protection (pantoprazole and sucralfate) and resuming home medications as tolerated. Plain films showed no free air or obstruction, and CT abdomen/pelvis with IV and oral contrast demonstrated normal-appearing anastomoses and appropriately positioned G-tube without obstruction, abscess, or other acute process. Diet was advanced and tolerated, nutrition assessment indicated oral intake >75% of requirements, and blood glucose remained within normal limits throughout hospitalization; she was discharged home ambulatory with oral ondansetron, continued PPI/sucralfate and dronabinol for appetite, limited liquid opioid for breakthrough pain, and instructions for outpatient hypoglycemia dietary management and follow-up.
